shots.title: HOW BIG IS A CELL, REALLY?
shots.purpose: Put the hidden scale on screen first: a single hair shaft crossing the frame with an unseen world at its edge
shots.claim: a human hair is about 80 micrometers wide and hides a microscopic universe
shots.evidence: full-bleed ink-wash hair shaft plate with faint organelle shapes hinted at the lower edge
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in along the hair: stillness first so the question lands clean
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the eye-limit macro

subject_contract.expected_subject: a single human hair shaft crossing the frame in vintage ink-wash style, faint microscopic world hinted beneath
required: one hair shaft crossing the frame

one_second.relationship: one strand of hair against an implied invisible world

shots.purpose: Show vision hitting its floor: measurement ticks fade out along the hair edge as detail dissolves
shots.claim: the naked eye resolves detail only down to about 0.1 millimeters
shots.evidence: macro plate of the hair edge with resolution ticks dissolving into blank wash
shots.motion_reason: slow drift along the edge toward the blur boundary

subject_contract.expected_subject: macro view of a hair shaft edge dissolving into blur, faint measurement ticks fading, vintage ink-wash style

one_second.relationship: detail dissolving past the eye's limit

shots.purpose: The signature move: one continuous dive through nested rings, hair to cell to mitochondrion to DNA
shots.claim: one continuous dive runs from hair width through a cell and a mitochondrion down to DNA at 2 nanometers
shots.evidence: plate of concentric nested rings shrinking toward a glowing center, largest ring hair-width scale, smallest a helix
shots.motion_reason: continuous zoom through the rings: the dive IS the explanation
shots.transition_reason: hard cut into the mitochondrion macro

subject_contract.expected_subject: concentric nested rings shrinking toward a small glowing double helix at center, vintage ink-wash parchment style

one_second.relationship: each ring is a world inside the last

shots.purpose: Macro detail of the working machinery: folded cristae burning sugar into ATP inside one organelle
shots.claim: a mitochondrion about 1 micrometer wide burns sugar into ATP inside folded cristae membranes
shots.evidence: full-bleed macro plate of one mitochondrion with warm glowing cristae folds
shots.motion_reason: slow push onto the cristae folds so the machinery reads as texture
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the DNA thread

subject_contract.expected_subject: one bean-shaped mitochondrion filling the frame with folded inner cristae, warm rust glow, vintage ink-wash style

one_second.relationship: folded machinery burning fuel inside a speck

shots.purpose: The absurd ratio made visible: a 2-meter thread coiled inside a cell, its width 2 nanometers
shots.claim: the DNA in one human cell uncoils to about 2 meters, yet the double helix is only 2 nanometers wide
shots.evidence: plate of a long coiled thread spilling out of a small cell outline, with a magnified helix segment at its end
shots.motion_reason: slow pan along the uncoiling thread, ending at the magnified helix
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the payoff hair shot

subject_contract.expected_subject: a long coiled thread spilling from a small cell outline with a magnified double-helix segment, vintage ink-wash parchment style
required: coiled thread spilling from a cell outline

one_second.relationship: two meters of thread coiled into a speck

shots.purpose: Payoff collapse: the ordinary hair back in warm light, its shadow now understood as 30 trillion nested worlds
shots.claim: the human body holds roughly 30 trillion cells, each a nested universe of unseen machines
shots.evidence: full-bleed plate of a single hair against warm light with a faint glowing universe of cells beneath
shots.motion_reason: slow pull-back to the quiet wide shot; the question resolves in one image

subject_contract.expected_subject: a single hair shaft in warm backlight with a faint field of glowing cells beneath it, vintage ink-wash style

one_second.relationship: the hair you know, now shadowing a universe
